market_question: Will Silver (SI) hit (HIGH) $120 by end of June?
reasoning: Silver at $120/oz (settlement ≥12000 cents) would be over double the all‑time nominal high of $49.45 and has never occurred even in inflation‑adjusted terms. With spot near $30 and only 15 months until resolution, the required quadrupling has no historical precedent outside hyperinflation. The market’s 6.7% probability grossly overstates this extreme‑tail chance.
evidence_points: Current silver spot ≈$30/oz; all‑time nominal high $49.45 (2011).
A move to $120 would be >2× the nominal record and >4× current price.
Resolution requires an official settlement print ≥12000.0, not just an intraday spike, further reducing the likelihood.
Even the inflation‑adjusted 1980 peak (~$175 in today’s dollars) was only reached in a unique speculative episode, not replicated in 45 years.
sources_consulted: CME Group Silver futures contract specifications (cents/troy oz settlement)
Historical silver prices (macrotrends.net, LBMA, Comex records)
US CPI inflation data for inflation‑adjusted highs
